answer.question: What should an Amelia City turf project consider first?
answer.answer: Choose the usable part of the yard and identify trees, drainage features and any waterfront restrictions. Amelia City is unincorporated Nassau County, so confirm the applicable county and community requirements for the address before finalizing the layout.

blocks.h2: Fit the green into a clearing you can reach.
paras: A putting green can leave the rest of a wooded lot intact. Choose the putts you want, the route from the house and room to walk around the surface. A lawn or pet area closer to the door can remain separate.
Mark tree canopy and roots before discussing preparation. Keep leaves and other debris in the care plan, and establish any required tree advice before proposing work beneath the canopy.

blocks.h2: Let the actual property set the boundary.
paras: On an Amelia River-facing lot, bring known shoreline and drainage information and show where water collects. Near the beach, identify any coastal or dune restrictions before placing the work area. A surface replacement alone will not resolve a wet-yard problem.

Use Nassau County requirements for an unincorporated parcel, plus the current rules of any private community. Do not assume Fernandina Beach’s historic review applies to the entire island or that a south-island address has no review at all.

blocks.h2: County rules here, not the city's design review.
paras: Amelia City is an unincorporated community on the south half of Amelia Island, so the City of Fernandina Beach's Land Development Code and its Historic District Council, with its Certificate of Appropriateness process, don't apply (Amelia City). Your turf job answers to Nassau County's development code and building department instead. That's a different path from the one a homeowner in the National Register district six miles north walks, not a lighter one: the county keeps a tree law written for this stretch of island alone.

That doesn't mean nobody reviews the yard. Plenty of south-end addresses sit inside private communities, Summer Beach, Amelia Island Plantation and Amelia Surf & Racquet Club among them, whose boards have a say on the color, height and edging of any turf, and on the beach side, state coastal-construction and dune-protection limits apply. Florida's Florida-Friendly Landscaping law won't override any of it, since it doesn't clearly protect synthetic turf (our guide to Florida-Friendly law and HOAs).

blocks.h2: The oaks set the edge of the base.
paras: Amelia City has a tree law the mainland doesn’t. On 9 August 2021 Nassau County adopted Ordinance No. 2021-012, § 37.02 of the county code, to limit the loss of trees in the unincorporated areas of Amelia Island (Nassau County). It went into effect on 7 February 2022 (ordinance summary). Fernandina Beach runs its own rules, and Nassauville across the river sits outside it altogether.

Two numbers shape a layout here. A protected tree is any healthy, non-invasive tree measuring 5 inches or more across the trunk at chest height, and removing one takes a county permit unless an exemption applies. A live oak of 40 inches or more is a specimen tree, and the county allows no exemption for those: removal needs the Nassau County-Amelia Island Tree Commission’s approval, on justification that the tree is dead, fallen or compromised, or that keeping it removes all economically viable use of the lot. Around every tree you keep there’s a protection zone of six times the trunk diameter, with a 6-foot minimum, and the county’s worked examples give a 10-inch trunk a 6-foot zone and a 20-inch trunk a 15-foot zone (ordinance summary).

Inside that zone the ordinance prohibits development activity: buildings, structures, paving surfaces, and temporary construction work including all digging, material storage and vehicle parking. Where the county engineer finds trenching or excavation inside the zone necessary for a tree being kept, it has to be bored or tunnelled instead of dug. Around protected trees the ordinance separately requires measures against grade changes, excavation, root compression and new impervious surfaces (ordinance summary). What the county doesn’t settle in writing is whether a residential turf base counts as development activity or as a new impervious surface. Email the county arborist at treeinfo@nassaucountyfl.com with a tree survey before the layout is fixed and put that question to them directly, because the answer to whether turf counts as impervious varies by jurisdiction.

blocks.h2: One day a week, whatever the water source.
paras: Water Shortage Order 2026-017 put the district’s portion of Nassau County, the unincorporated south island included, under a Phase III Extreme Water Shortage. The district declared it on 13 May 2026 (SJRWMD) and said it was still in effect on 3 September 2026: a single irrigation day each week, Saturday for an odd or no street number and Sunday for an even one, nothing between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., and aesthetic water use banned (SJRWMD watering restrictions).

If you're on the public system out here it's Nassau Amelia, largely south of A1A, which moved from Nassau County to the Florida Governmental Utility Authority on 18 September 2025, so the bill comes from FGUA and not the City of Fernandina Beach utility (FGUA). FGUA publishes no schedule of its own and sends customers to the water management district and the county instead (FGUA water restrictions). Some south-end parcels are on wells instead, and the restrictions cover private wells and pumps as well as utility water (SJRWMD watering restrictions), so check what your address actually runs on.

Outside a shortage, the district allows twice-weekly watering in daylight saving time and once-weekly in winter (SJRWMD). No rebate for artificial turf is on offer from the water management district. Turf simply drops off the watering schedule.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Amelia City, FL?
faq.a: We install artificial lawns, pet turf and putting greens in Amelia City, FL, on the south end of Amelia Island. Amelia City is unincorporated, so Nassau County's code applies rather than Fernandina Beach's and its Historic District Council. Many lots face the Amelia River across tidal marsh, where the water table runs high, so the base and drainage decide the job. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: Is Amelia City part of Fernandina Beach?
faq.a: No. Amelia City is an unincorporated community on the south half of Amelia Island, along A1A near the Amelia River, so Nassau County, not the city, sets the rules (Amelia City). Fernandina Beach is the island's only incorporated city.

faq.q: Will turf drain on a lot that backs onto the marsh?
faq.a: Yes, with a base designed for a high water table. West-side lots near the Amelia River sit on the poorly drained soils Nassau County's comprehensive plan flags, so base depth and drainage matter more than the turf you choose (Nassau County). We check the lot on the free visit.

faq.q: Do trees on my lot need a permit before turf goes in?
faq.a: Only if a protected tree has to come out. On unincorporated Amelia Island, § 37.02 protects any healthy, non-invasive tree of 5 inches or more across the trunk, and removing one takes a county permit (ordinance summary). The county exempts dead, fallen and diseased trees, storm emergencies, routine pruning done to ISA and ANSI standards, and anything under 5 inches, and state law keeps local permitting off a tree a certified arborist has documented as an unacceptable risk to people or property (Nassau County). What usually shapes a turf layout is the protection zone around the trees you keep: six times the trunk diameter, 6-foot minimum, with development activity and digging barred inside it. Email treeinfo@nassaucountyfl.com with a tree survey before the plan is fixed, and ask how the county treats a turf base inside that zone.

On the public system it's Nassau Amelia, largely south of A1A, run by the Florida Governmental Utility Authority since 18 September 2025 rather than by the county (FGUA). FGUA sets no irrigation days itself and sends customers to the water management district and the county (FGUA water restrictions). Some parcels out here are on wells instead, so read your own bill before you assume either way.
